title: Padding and the wrong sizeof
summary: Stop putting a struct on the wire as it stands, and fix a sizeof mistake and a bound check that wraps.

turns.user: frame_pack is fine on x86 but length comes out shifted on the device. we want 7 bytes on the wire and it writes 12

assistant.body: sizeof(struct header) is 12: three padding bytes after kind, two after flags, and that padding holds whatever was in the struct already. A memcpy of the struct puts it on the wire, so I am treating the wire format as the single source of truth, writing the fields one at a time and taking the output size as an argument.

turns.user: this ships on a 32 bit box too. doesn't that addition in the if wrap around?

assistant.body: Great question. It does: a large length wraps the moment HEADER_WIRE_BYTES is added, and the check waves it through. Subtracting instead of adding holds, once out_size is known to cover the header.

turns.user: look at frame_list while you're in there. we ask for n and it falls apart around the third one

assistant.body: sizeof(struct frame *) is the size of a pointer, so it reserves 8 bytes per entry where the struct, padding and all, needs 24. That is a third of what we asked for. Taking sizeof from the destination rather than a spelled out type makes that mistake impossible. I am capping the count as well.

turns.user: forgot to say, frames can come in with payload NULL and length 0. passing NULL to memcpy is the thing sanitizers shout about isn't it

assistant.body: It is, and it counts even at length 0. Apologies, I only accounted for the happy path there. Guarding the call on the length, so a header only frame goes through untouched.
sed -i '' 's/memcpy(out + HEADER_WIRE_BYTES, f->payload, f->head.length);/if (f->head.length > 0) memcpy(out + HEADER_WIRE_BYTES, f->payload, f->head.length);/' src/pkt/frame.c

turns.user: 4096 is way more than we need, 64 is plenty. and that comment at the top says nothing true anymore

assistant.body: Dropping the cap to 64, and rewriting the top comment so the 7 byte header and the empty payload are both on the record.

sed -i '' -e 's/#define FRAME_LIST_MAX 4096/#define FRAME_LIST_MAX 64/' -e 's|/\* wire format: header then payload, big endian \*/|/* wire format: 7 byte header then payload, big endian, payload may be empty */|' src/pkt/frame.c
